findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument
findings.body: In `UsernameForm.authenticate()` the expression `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` invokes a zero-argument method, but the only declaration of that name in the inheritance hierarchy is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (added in this PR in UsernamePasswordForm.java at line 160). There is no no-arg overload and no static import of one, so the project will not compile and the build will fail. The intended call is almost certainly `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, mirroring how the helper is used in UsernamePasswordForm.java.

findings.title: Unreachable assertion: driver.findElement throws before the matcher can run
findings.body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()` the pattern `try { MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }` does not actually assert absence. Selenium's `driver.findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` as soon as the element is missing, so the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` and `fail(...)` lines are unreachable and the catch block silently swallows the exception. The same try/catch is duplicated around line 311. The tests therefore pass regardless of whether the webauthn form is really absent. Use `driver.findElements(...)` and assert the resulting list is empty.

findings.title: WebAuthn form data not populated for initial login (user not yet identified)
findings.body: In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` the new guard `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` requires `user != null`, because the helper at line 160 is `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The previous code path called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever passkeys were enabled, regardless of whether a user was already in the context. The new check therefore skips `fillContextForm` for the user-null branch (initial login, no user yet identified), so the login page no longer receives the WebAuthn challenge (`AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE`), `CHALLENGE`, `RP_ID`, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` and friends. The new tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` in PasskeysUsernameFormTest and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest both call `oauth.openLoginForm()` with no user yet identified and immediately expect a successful passkey login (`appPage.assertCurrent()`); without the server-side challenge the WebAuthn response cannot be verified and those tests will fail. The accompanying comment "setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled" also no longer matches the implemented condition, which additionally requires the user to be identified.
